thread:
Amira: Heads-up — product asked us to add tenant_id + kms_key_id + caller_role to the audit event schema so customers can map actions to their KMS usage. We need to think about volume/cost and validation for customer-facing events. Any quick takes?
Jon: That's a big signal. Two immediate concerns: index cardinality and per-event metadata causing size blowup. We should sketch retention and tiering first. :thinking:
Sachin: Agreed. Also need to decide if we store kms_key_id as plaintext in the event index or only in encrypted blob. Storing as searchable field increases index size.
Maria: From CS: customers expect to see which key was used when they review audits (esp enterprise). They want it searchable in the UI.
Priya: For compliance teams, searchable is important. Maybe we can keep a small searchable field (key alias) and put full details in the encrypted payload.
Amira: Proposal: add a short key_alias (max 64 chars) as a top-level string for indexing, and put full kms metadata inside encrypted payload. That gives the customer what they need without exposing raw key fingerprints. Thoughts on ingestion cost?
Jon: If we add tenant_id + key_alias to every event, per-event doc size grows. Estimate: current avg audit event 800 bytes. Adding fields + index overhead ~+120 bytes -> +15% storage. For 100M events/month that's ~12 GB extra. On ES that could be more due to segments. We should evaluate batching and compression.
Sachin: We can also compress payloads (gzip) and send events in batches to the ingest pipeline. Batching reduces per-request overhead and KMS calls if you're doing envelope encryption.
Priya: Important: customers will query by tenant_id in UI filters. We must index tenant_id (keyword). But we can make other fields optional indexed.
Amira: Ops question: for KMS integration, do we call customer KMS per event? That would blow up API calls and cost.
Jon: Don't call KMS per event. Use envelope encryption: generate a single data key per batch (or per minute window), encrypt payloads with that local key, then call KMS once to encrypt the data-key and store the ciphertext key with the batch metadata. That reduces KMS QPS dramatically.
Sachin: Example pseudo-flow:
```
# batch handling example
batch = collect(events)
datakey = crypto.generate_data_key()
encrypted_payloads = [crypto.aes_gcm_encrypt(datakey, e) for e in batch]
kms_cipher = KMS.encrypt(customer_key_id, datakey)
store(batch_meta={kms_ciphertext:kms_cipher, key_alias:alias}, payloads=compressed(encrypted_payloads))
```
Amira: Nice. Also need to surface to customers which events were sampled if we do sampling. They may misinterpret missing events.
Maria: Customer-facing validation: they asked for a signed audit event dump they can ingest into their SIEM. We need a deterministic signed export format and a validation endpoint that verifies the signature and schema.
Priya: So we should attach an HMAC signature per-export file (sign with service key) and include manifest.json with checksums + schema version. For live UI, we can show 'validated' badges if the signature checks.
Jon: Backpressure scenario: if ingest pipeline lags, we need throttling signals to clients. Use HTTP 429 with Retry-After, and have ingest-bot post alerts to #eng-oncall. Also track queue_depth, write_latency, and batch_retry_count as metrics per-tenant.
ingest-bot: ALERT: write_lag > 90th pct threshold for audit-ingest-01, starting controlled throttling for non-critical tenants.
Amira: For prioritization: designate two QoS classes — audit-critical (SLA customers) and best-effort. Critical tenants go to a hot write path with higher cost but guaranteed ingest. Best-effort can be sampled/aggregated under pressure.
Sachin: Indexing strategy: hot ES indexes for last 30 days with tenant shards sharded by tenant_hash prefix; cold storage (Parquet on S3 or ClickHouse) for longer retention. This reduces long-term ES cost.
Jon: Also consider storing a compact 'search index' document with only indexed fields (tenant_id, timestamp, actor, action, key_alias) to serve UI queries, and keep full payloads in compressed blobs for forensic retrieval. That reduces index size while keeping searchability.
Amira: That sounds like a good compromise. Contractual note: for legal / e-discovery requests we must be able to reconstruct full event including kms metadata — ensure key rotation + replay works.
Priya: Key rotation: keep a key rotation table mapping old_kms_ciphertext -> rewrapped_with_new_key, or reencrypt datakey on rotation. We need a migration plan documented.
Maria: CS follow-up: can we provide a sample export for customers that demonstrates schema + signed manifest? If yes, customers will be happier.
Amira: I'll draft a sample schema and signed export flow. Quick schema sketch:
```
{
  "schema_version": "2026-01-01",
  "tenant_id": "tenant_123",
  "timestamp": "2026-01-12T15:04:05Z",
  "actor": "service-account:x",
  "action": "model.deploy",
  "key_alias": "cust-prod-key-1",
  "payload_ref": "s3://audit-blobs/2026/01/12/batch-0001.gz",
  "event_id": "evt_abc123",
  "caller_role": "admin"
}
```
Sachin: Also attach fields for sampling_note when event was downsampled: {sampled: true, sampling_rate: 0.01} so users know coverage.
Jon: Cost calc: if we keep searchable compact docs ~200 bytes + full compressed blobs averaging 400 bytes per event in batch, effective storage ~600 bytes. 100M events -> ~60 GB/month raw. With ES overhead maybe ~2-3x. Need to price vs S3 cold-only approach. We'll sketch TCO for next sync.
Priya: Security triage: if we change schema, run vuln scan on serialization libs, watch for object injection, and add schema validation at ingest to reject malformed events.
Amira: Action items: 1) I will produce a short RFC with schema + envelope-encryption batch design + retention tiers. 2) Jon to model index cost (ES vs compact index + blobs) and ingestion QPS. 3) Sachin to prototype batch datakey flow and show KMS calls per batch. 4) Maria to prepare customer export example and wording about sampling.
devops-bot: NOTE: created issue SEC-AUDIT-2026 for RFC and linked to eng-infra board.
Amira: Thanks — I'll tag people in the RFC draft. If anyone has data points (current avg audit size, peak qps per tenant) drop them here.
Jon: I'll send a quick spreadsheet with size and cost scenarios by EOD.
Maria: I'll collect top 5 enterprise asks for searchable fields.
Sachin: I'll spin up a small prototype today for datakey per-batch encrypt.
Amira: Great — wrapping up. We'll aim to present options in next week's sync. :thumbsup:
